Here, we let $u(x)={x}^{2}+4x$ and $v(x)=arccscx,$ and apply the quotient rule.

We use the formulae

$$
{u}^{′}(x)=2x+4\,\text{and}\,{v}^{′}(x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(2x+4)\cdot arccscx-({x}^{2}+4x)\cdot (-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}})}{{arccsc}^{2}x} \\  & =\frac{2x+4}{arccscx}+\frac{{x}^{2}+4x}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}\cdot {arccsc}^{2}x}.\end{aligned}
$$
